headline: What Has The Market Missed In Lululemon Stock's Drop?
summary: Lululemon Athletica (LULU) continues to quietly absorb its own shares, a trend the current stock price appears to ignore. Investors generally view the athletic apparel maker as a leggings brand dealing with stalled sales. The stock lost 41.4% over the past twelve months, while the S&P 500 returned 17.9%. Yet the company steadily reduced its share count alongside that falling valuation, setting up a sharp contradiction. So how much of its own stock is Lululemon buying back.

headline: What Is Going On With PepsiCo Stock?
summary: PepsiCo (PEP) stock trades at 16.1 times earnings. The median S&P 500 company, by contrast, trades at 22.8 times earnings. Over the past year, PepsiCo shares lost 11.9%, while the S&P 500 returned 17.9%. This underperformance occurred even as the company posted higher sales, margins, and cash flow in the twelve months to September 5, 2026. The market is either overlooking an improving business, or accurately pricing a company with stalled growth. What does a buyer get at this price.

headline: Does The Move In Snowflake Stock Change Anything?
summary: Snowflake (SNOW) stock rose 59.3% from January 18 to October 15, 2026, against 12.5% for the S&P 500. So how much faster is Snowflake growing than it was in January.

headline: What Is The Biggest Threat To Microsoft Stock?
